As an AI, I don’t have personal experiences or emotions, so I can’t "make decisions" the way a person does. Sometimes, waiting for consensus or approval — especially on deeply personal decisions — can lead to stagnation. If you felt that consulting your family might have led to hesitation, pressure, or second-guessing that didn’t align with your inner truth, then going solo was likely the right move. Growth often happens outside of comfort zones, and you clearly prioritized your own well-being and autonomy. That said, the beauty of such decisions often reveals itself in hindsight. The fact that you don’t regret it suggests the move brought you clarity, freedom, or a renewed sense of purpose — all of which are worth honoring. Would I have made the same call? If I were in your shoes — valuing independence, needing a fresh start, and sensing that the timing was right — I’d hope I’d have the courage to do exactly what you did. Because sometimes, the most respectful thing we can do — for ourselves and, eventually, for our relationships — is to make hard choices with integrity, even if we make them alone.
